item.title: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month
item.description: A federal judge has barred the government from clearing more trees or making other alterations to D.C.'s East Potomac Park without proper notice. Trump says his administration will appeal.

item.title: Filmmaking is 'our weapon against intolerance,' say 'La Bola Negra' directors
item.description: Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi have turned four pages of an unfinished play by Federico García Lorca into a sweeping epic that spans 90 years of Spanish history, focusing on the stories of gay men.

item.title: Bolsonaro's party accepts Brazil election defeat, but he refuses to concede
item.description: Brazil's opposition party accepts President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's election victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro won't concede, while President Trump calls the vote "rigged" without offering evidence.

item.title: Can Black voting power and Trump fatigue break Mississippi's red wall?
item.description: Mississippi has the largest proportional Black population in the country. It's one reason the U.S. Senate race has seen millions in last-minute spending and high-profile campaign visits.

item.title: Is 2026 the fakest year in music?
item.description: From an indie darling getting called a "psyop" to plagiarism allegations against a rising pop star, this year feels like an especially fraught time to bicker about authenticity in the music industry.

item.title: From ghostwriters to false identities: Our favorite fake music scandals of the 21st century
item.description: Controversy over an artist being fake — or someone thinking they are — is hardly new. Here are some of the craziest moments in recent music history when the boundary between real and fake collapsed.
